name: team_planning_capacity
description: Get the capacity of a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in. Each person is a seat, and so is each position for the FTE its occupants leave open. Each place a seat holds (a unit or a position, and its share of the seat) is priced by the capacity model its role chooses through the capacity_model planning rule, a role's choice beating its family's. A place in a position takes the position's role and level; a person placed straight in a unit takes those their title and level map to. An allocation the HRIS didn't give (allocation_known false) shares what the seat's other places leave. Each figure carries its working. Totals are per model, per unit and for the scenario, never summed across models; a place in a unit gone from the map counts for the scenario only. A place no model covers counts nowhere and is listed in `unclassified` with its reason. Each working step has an op (+, × or =) and, where it charges for someone or an open seat, a subject_id. A figure is overloaded when what the seat costs to manage beats its base, by `excess`, and its notes say what a reader should know, such as an open seat that counts against no manager. A planner's override (team_planning_set_capacity_override) replaces a place's capacity, its working ends with the override, and `calculated` carries the model's figure, with that figure's overloaded, excess and notes in `calculated_diagnostics` while the top-level ones describe the planner's figure. An override the plan can't read, since its person was forgotten, leaves the place unclassified with the model's figure still in `calculated`. `overridden` marks every place the plan holds an override for, so one on a place that counts nowhere for another reason, such as a leaver's, stays visible. Figures are decimal strings. `models` maps each model a place uses to its symbol, what follows its figures on screen, and its description. People are named by id, and `names` maps each to a name. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: The scenario, or the plan's id for the baseline.
